turns.question: i am an employee of a board of park commissioners, how is my pension calculated?
turns.answer:
**Needs information**

Your pension must be calculated under Article 12, but your fund must correct your record from Article 11 first. The salary and service currently on file are not the right basis for an Article 12 calculation.

You told me you are an employee of a board of park commissioners. Article 12 provides a fixed-benefit annuity for an employee who withdraws on or after December 31, 2003, at age 50 or over with at least 10 years of service, or at age 60 or over with at least 4 years of service. The formula is 2.40% for each year of service, based on your highest average annual salary for any 4 consecutive years within the last 10 years before withdrawal. The annuity is capped at 80% of that average salary. If retirement is before age 60, the Code generally reduces the annuity by 1/4 of 1% for each month or fraction of a month before age 60. The reduction does not apply if you retire at age 50 or over with at least 30 years of service. [40 ILCS 5/12-133]

The earlier fixed-benefit rates apply only to withdrawals before December 31, 2003, so they are not the provision used here. The accumulation-based provisions in Sections 12-133(b) and 12-130 apply only to employees who entered service before July 1, 1971, so they do not apply here.

To put a figure on your Article 12 pension, your fund must first correct the Article 11 record. After that, the needed information is: What is your age at withdrawal from service? How many years of service you have with the fund, and your salary for each of the last ten years, or your best four consecutive years. Your date of birth is also needed to determine any reduction for retirement before age 60.

turns.question: i thought park employee's came under article 12, is it correct, if not what type of employees come under article 12?
turns.answer:
Yes, some park employees come under Article 12, but the job title alone does not decide it. Your record places your own pension under Article 11 — tell me if that is not right.

Article 12 covers employees of a board of park commissioners, including classified-service and exempt employees, and employees of that board’s retirement board. Its coverage test excludes positions requiring less than 90 hours in a month, or, beginning July 1, 1991, less than 6 months in a calendar year, unless the person is already a fund member. It also excludes a city or district employee transferred to a park district under the Exchange of Functions Act of 1957. [40 ILCS 5/12-118] Article 12 also preserves coverage for eligible park-district employees, other than park policemen, who were transferred to a city under that Act and were already members of the fund. [40 ILCS 5/12-119] Your own pension is administered under Article 11, so your salary and service are not the figures to use for an Article 12 calculation.

turns.question: What does Section 11-134 say about the annuity formula?
turns.answer:
Section 11-134 provides several annuity formulas. For a qualifying employee with at least 20 years of service, the formula generally uses the highest average annual salary over either 4 or 5 consecutive years in the last 10 years of service. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

- One formula uses tiered percentages for different portions of your service: 1.67% for the first 10 years, 1.90% for the next 10 years, 2.10% for service over 20 through 30 years, and 2.30% for service over 30 years.
- Another formula is available by election and uses 2.40% for each year of service for a withdrawal on or after January 1, 2002. It is based on the highest average annual salary for 4 consecutive years in the last 10 years. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]
- Section 11-134 also provides a 2.40%-per-year elected formula for employees with at least 10 years of service who withdraw on or after January 1, 1999. That annuity begins no earlier than age 60 and is subject to the stated maximum. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]
- Depending on the formula and your retirement age, the annuity may be reduced by 0.25% for each month, or fractional part of a month, that commencement is before age 60. The statute waives that reduction in specified cases involving age and years of service. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

No dollar amount can be stated here because no annuity calculation was worked out this turn. To work one out, the applicable withdrawal date, the formula you elect if more than one applies, and whether the statutory age-and-service exception to the reduction applies would be needed.

turns.question: What retirement annuity does Article 8 provide for a police officer with 25 years?
turns.answer:
Article 8 does not provide one single retirement annuity simply because a police officer has 25 years of service. It provides several possible annuity provisions, depending on the employee’s age, withdrawal date, salary history, and election.

A police officer’s service is counted as city employee service under Article 8. For service after the effective date, the required employee contributions must also have been paid, and the same period cannot retain credit in another city police, firefighter, or teacher pension fund. [40 ILCS 5/8-227]

For an employee with at least 20 years of service, Article 8 includes minimum-annuity provisions based on the highest average annual salary for four consecutive years in the last 10 years of service. Some provisions apply at age 60 or older. Other provisions permit an election beginning at age 55, or at age 50 with at least 30 years of service, with an early-retirement reduction unless an exception applies. The Code also includes different rules for employees with at least 25 years of service who retire at age 55 or older but younger than age 60. [40 ILCS 5/8-138]

The annuity is also subject to Article 8’s maximum-annuity limits. The exact Article 8 amount cannot be worked out here because the applicable retirement date, the employee’s election, and the required salary basis are not provided. [40 ILCS 5/8-154]

Your own pension is recorded under Article 11, not Article 8. The part not answered by the Pension Code here is any tax or insurance treatment; that belongs to the IRS or the fund’s administrative staff.
